announcements.name: Maia 200 and Cobalt 200 silicon
announcements.shortDescription: Next-generation in-house chips for AI processing (Maia) and Arm-based agent workloads (Cobalt), extending the line first announced three years prior
announcements.longDescription: Continuing server-side infrastructure innovation, Microsoft announced the Maia 200 and Cobalt 200, successors to the Maia and Cobalt chips first announced three years prior. Maia is a chipset designed to optimize AI processing, while Cobalt uses an Arm-based architecture optimized for agent applications. The emphasis is on executing workloads efficiently across both edge and infrastructure, framed around performance-per-watt and token efficiency.

announcements.name: Azure HorizonDB [inferred] public preview
announcements.shortDescription: A managed, PostgreSQL-compatible open-source database supporting large-scale OLTP, alongside Cosmos DB on the backend
announcements.longDescription: As part of innovating the database layer, Microsoft highlighted Azure HorizonDB [inferred] ("Horazon David") as a newer technology released in public preview. It is described as a PostgreSQL-compatible [inferred] open-source database used by many customers that supports even large-scale OLTP processing in a managed fashion. This complements existing backends like Cosmos DB used on the ChatGPT backend.

announcements.name: GPU-accelerated Fabric Data Warehouse
announcements.shortDescription: Using NVIDIA accelerated computing to deliver up to 7x query performance with no application changes
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced GPU acceleration for the Fabric data warehouse, built on NVIDIA accelerated computing. By combining accelerated computing with parallel processing, query performance can be increased by up to 7 times. A key point is that this high-speed data warehouse can be realized without changing the existing application running on Fabric.

announcements.name: Web IQ and Work IQ API GA
announcements.shortDescription: Adds web grounding optimized for agents to the existing Work/Public/Foundry IQ family, with the Work IQ API reaching general availability
announcements.longDescription: In addition to the existing Work IQ, Public IQ, and Foundry IQ family, Microsoft presented Web IQ, an engine optimized for agent processing that supports web grounding, doing so faster and at lower cost than previously possible. The transcript also notes that customers want to use this capability in their own applications, and a key point is that the Work IQ API actually reaches general availability (GA).

announcements.name: Microsoft Execution Container (MXC)
announcements.shortDescription: A sandboxed runtime for safely executing agent actions (e.g., the OpenClaw [inferred] computer-use agent), with native binaries and a TypeScript SDK published on GitHub. [00:09:43]
announcements.longDescription: The Microsoft Execution Container (MXC) is a sandboxed runtime that lets agents run safely and securely, used in keynotes to run OpenClaw [inferred] on Windows and also underpinning the Copilot SDK. MXC implements a native binary for the OS layer, and the SDK for the interface to that native binary is implemented in TypeScript. This is publicly available on GitHub as a preview of the service.

announcements.name: Host agent
announcements.shortDescription: A server-side foundation for scaling and securely running agents
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft announced the host agent as a foundation for running agents on the server side. As agents increasingly need to run and scale, the open agent architecture executes on top of this host agent foundation so agents can be scaled and run securely. Offering this kind of environment is presented as a major point.

announcements.name: Microsoft Scout
announcements.shortDescription: An autonomous "Autopilot" agent demoed in Japanese performing expense reimbursement across M365 cloud and local data, with the final decision left to a human
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft Scout is an autonomous "Autopilot" agent, demonstrated in Japanese performing a business trip expense reimbursement task. It simultaneously searches M365 cloud data and local data to find files, analyzes them to extract reimbursement content, and enters the data into the user's usual expense application. The agent takes the lead but leaves the final decision to a human for safety and security, with Microsoft Scout uploading files and completing the settlement.

announcements.name: Microsoft AI models
announcements.shortDescription: Seven models presented by Mustafa Suleyman [inferred], including image (MAI Image 2.5 [inferred]) and a reasoning model (MAI Thinking [inferred]); plus frontier tuning for domain-specific optimization
announcements.longDescription: Presented by Mustafa Suleyman [inferred], founder of DeepMind and now leader of the Microsoft AI effort, Microsoft released seven different models. Examples include an image model (MAI Image 2.5 [inferred]) for image optimization and a high-accuracy character recognition model, with the most emphasized being a reasoning-based standard model (MAI Thinking [inferred]). Microsoft also presented frontier tuning, which optimizes a model using a company's own domain knowledge, all within the Microsoft Foundry that supports over 11,000 models.

announcements.name: Agent 365 Local Agent and SDK
announcements.shortDescription: Management of locally running agents as corporate assets, plus an SDK for building governed agents in any environment
announcements.longDescription: Building on the previously announced Agent 365, Microsoft introduced Agent 365 Local Agent, which allows management of agents running locally, such as on employee PCs, treating them as important corporate assets to detect risks and reduce exposure. Alongside it, the Agent 365 SDK lets developers create agents in any kind of environment while controlling them properly on the control plane. The motivation is governing organizations where individuals and a rapidly growing number of agents merge.

announcements.name: Microsoft Discovery (GA) and Majorana 2 [inferred]
announcements.shortDescription: Research-exploration services for drug/chemical discovery and quantum computing progress targeting 2029. [00:20:00]
announcements.longDescription: Under the "Beyond the Frontier" theme, Microsoft announced Microsoft Discovery, now GA, a research-exploration service optimized for areas such as drug discovery and chemical substances, applying AI to generate and repeatedly test hypotheses. Microsoft also highlighted progress in quantum computing with the Majorana 2 [inferred] chip, improving reliability and minimizing error rates, with capabilities targeted to become reality in 2029.

announcements.name: GitHub Copilot desktop app and Copilot SDK GA
announcements.shortDescription: Enterprise agentic development with a Canvas extension, daily automation running in the cloud, and SDK support for six languages (Java and another newly added). [00:29:00]
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft launched the Copilot SDK at GA, enabling enterprise agentic development where AI agent teams and humans collaborate toward a single outcome. In the Copilot desktop app, tasks can be assigned, looped, code-reviewed in a split pane, and automatically merged by agents. The SDK currently supports six languages, with Java and a final language newly added, and includes cross-platform and sandbox functions so agents can run on local machines, in the cloud, or in network-disconnected environments.

announcements.name: Foundry IQ serverless
announcements.shortDescription: Serverless AI search in public preview, scaling to zero, with a developer tier
announcements.longDescription: Foundry IQ serverless was announced in public preview as a serverless AI search service. Whereas the previous AI search system required sizing capacity in advance, the serverless model can scale to zero, making it more user-friendly. It is currently available in a developer tier for trial use.

announcements.name: Foundry observability and optimization
announcements.shortDescription: New multi-turn Evaluation and continuous evaluation (public preview); Rubric Evaluator, Agent Optimizer, and ROI for Agents (private preview)
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft introduced new Foundry evaluation and observability capabilities, validated by NTT DATA during private preview. The new Evaluation capability extends existing functions to support multi-turn evaluations across full conversational exchanges, dataset creation from existing trace data, and continuous evaluation with sampling, released as public preview. In private preview, the Rubric Evaluator automatically generates custom evaluators from agent definitions, and an Agent Optimizer (plus ROI for Agents) builds on the rubric evaluator.

announcements.name: Fairwater AI data center and Project Leyfin [inferred]
announcements.shortDescription: A dedicated AI data center built on sustainability principles, and a Fabric-powered service (public preview) for taking AI apps to production including backend. [00:41:00]
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft began construction of an AI-dedicated data center called Fairwater, built on sustainability principles such as not raising local electricity bills and circulating water to reduce consumption toward zero, and running Microsoft's in-house Maia and Cobalt chips. Separately, Project Leyfin [inferred] is a Fabric-powered service that helps take AI apps and mockups to production level—including the difficult backend work of authentication, operations, and governance—and was announced as a public preview.

announcements.name: GitHub Copilot app modernization
announcements.shortDescription: Expanded scenarios including mainframe migration, validated with partners Hitachi and NTT Data
announcements.longDescription: GitHub Copilot app modernization was presented as a feature extension (not a GA) aimed at changing how modernization progresses by helping development, infrastructure, and IT teams work on the same foundation. Demonstrated via a VS Code extension on a Java application, it runs an assessment in roughly 20 minutes that reports how to migrate to the cloud and what needs to change. The biggest change in the announcement is expanding supported scenarios to include mainframe migration, with the work validated alongside Japanese partners such as Hitachi and NTT Data.
